claims.text: Nickel-based alloys can be used to prepare parts for hot-dip aluminum plating equipment.
Iron-based alloys can be used to prepare parts for hot-dip aluminum plating equipment.
High-temperature corrosion-resistant nickel- or iron-based alloys protect equipment from erosion by liquid aluminum.
Sinking rollers, pulling rollers, and guide plates are initially made of unspecified common materials.
Replacing common materials with corrosion-resistant nickel- or iron-based alloys changes the material used for equipment components.
Hot-dip aluminum plating exposes the equipment to a high-temperature environment.
The alloys' microstructure and composition mediate their corrosion behavior.
Alloying or material selection can provide a barrier against corrosion by liquid aluminum.
Using the proposed corrosion-resistant alloys will reduce equipment corrosion.
Using the proposed corrosion-resistant alloys will increase equipment service life.
Performance depends on the temperature and duration of exposure to liquid aluminum.
A comparison against equipment made from common materials can test the proposed alloy substitution.
Failure to produce a significant service-life increase or corrosion-rate reduction relative to common materials would falsify the hypothesis.
